summary: Feed s101_single to IDS is degraded due to high encrypted traffic share (70.7% vs 60% IDS tolerance). All other checks (duplicates, VLANs, one-way, oversize, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: 71% of bytes are TLS/encrypted and delivered to IDS without prior decryption. IDS needs full cleartext payload for signature and anomaly detection, but traffic is increasingly encrypted upstream of the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect encrypted payloads, reducing detection coverage for exploits, C2 and malware inside TLS; only metadata/flow analysis remains effective, creating blind spot for ~11% excess encrypted traffic above tolerance.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires cleartext to match signatures. Provide selective TLS decryption via visibility/SSL inspection zone before IDS or feed a decrypted copy from packet broker to restore payload visibility while respecting privacy policy.
